title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
abstract: arXiv:2608.03874v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Modern agent frameworks equip large language models with external skill libraries to solve complex tasks. However, it remains unclear whether these systems can effectively evolve their skills and whether the resulting skills improve task-solving capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce ContinualSkillBench, a dynamic evaluation framework for in-context continual skill learning. It covers five domains, each with 100 tasks ordered by difficulty and opportunities for skill transfer. Our experiments show that sequential execution generally improves performance, but the gains vary substantially across models and domains. Moreover, across two models and three domains, retaining context and feedback without skill maintenance yields nearly the same mean performance as maintaining an explicit skill library. Explicit skills nevertheless provide selective benefits for tasks requiring reusable procedures or precise outputs. We further find

translated_title: ContinualSkillBench：LLM智能体能否真正进化其能力？
translated_abstract: 现代智能体框架为大语言模型配备外部技能库以解决复杂任务。然而，这些系统能否有效地进化其技能，以及由此产生的技能能否提升任务解决能力，仍不清楚。为了弥补这一空白，我们引入了ContinualSkillBench，一个用于上下文内持续技能学习的动态评估框架。它涵盖五个领域，每个领域包含按难度排序的100个任务以及技能迁移的机会。我们的实验表明，顺序执行通常能提升性能，但收益在不同模型和领域之间差异显著。此外，在两个模型和三个领域的实验中，仅保留上下文和反馈而不进行技能维护，其平均性能与维护显式技能库几乎相同。尽管如此，显式技能对于需要可复用流程或精确输出的任务仍能提供选择性的收益。我们进一步发现……
tldr: 该论文提出动态评估框架ContinualSkillBench，用于衡量LLM智能体的上下文内持续技能学习能力，发现顺序执行通常提升性能但收益因模型和领域而异，且显式技能库仅在需要可复用流程或精确输出的任务中带来选择性收益。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces ContinualSkillBench, a dynamic evaluation framework for in-context continual skill learning of LLM agents, showing that sequential execution generally improves performance with substantial variation across models and domains, and that explicit skill libraries only provide selective benefits for tasks requiring reusable procedures or precise outputs.
